source.value:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/5e03c481312af462a0739b4670e24325d2e06cc10449c65bfb04208206fc5d58.png)
Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda  & 5 \\ -1 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
$\lambda_1={\color{red}-1}.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 5}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 2\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/712c3f663a367090ab5ba81705e7c7f36ce6d4e2d6e2b13cc59383421e408ea7.png)
